_comment: Every popover follows the same contract: a plain definition, why it matters here, then a real source. Glossary lives as data so the same wording is reused by the page, the console and the README.

antibiogram.title: Antibiogram
antibiogram.plain: A summary of which antibiotics still work against the bacteria found in this specific hospital.
antibiogram.why: National averages can look very different from what is actually growing in one small town. Prescribing against the wrong picture is how the wrong drug gets chosen.
antibiogram.source: CLSI M39, Analysis and Presentation of Cumulative Antimicrobial Susceptibility Test Data

empiric.title: Empiric therapy
empiric.plain: The antibiotic a doctor starts before anyone knows which bacteria is causing the infection.
empiric.why: It is an educated guess, made because waiting two days for the lab could be dangerous. The guess is usually broad on purpose.
empiric.source: CDC Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship

deescalation.title: De-escalation
deescalation.plain: Switching from a broad antibiotic to a narrower one once the lab identifies the bacteria.
deescalation.why: Narrower drugs do less damage to the body's own bacteria and slow the spread of resistance. Guidelines recommend reviewing this at 48 to 72 hours.
deescalation.source: Epidemiology and Outcomes of Broad-Spectrum Antibiotic De-escalation

susceptible.title: Susceptible, S
susceptible.plain: The lab tested this antibiotic against this bacteria and it worked.
susceptible.why: Only S counts as susceptible. Intermediate results are counted in the total but not as a success, which is why a percentage can be lower than it first appears.

resistant.title: Resistant, R
resistant.plain: The lab tested this antibiotic against this bacteria and it did not work.
resistant.why: If a patient is on a drug the bacteria is resistant to, the treatment is probably doing nothing. That is the urgent case this system looks for.

first-isolate.title: First isolate rule
first-isolate.plain: Only the first time a given bacteria is found in a given patient counts toward the summary.
first-isolate.why: Without this rule, one very sick patient tested ten times would dominate the hospital's picture. CLSI applies it regardless of which part of the body the sample came from.

suppressed.title: Why some cells show no number
suppressed.plain: Fewer than 30 samples were tested, so no percentage is shown at all.
suppressed.why: A percentage from a handful of samples is misleading. CLSI requires at least 30 before reporting a rate, and there is published analysis of how unreliable small numbers are.
suppressed.source: Estimated Impact of Low Isolate Numbers on the Reliability of Cumulative Antibiogram Data

simulated-clock.title: Simulated clock
simulated-clock.plain: A control that moves this demo's clock forward so you can watch five weeks happen in a minute.
simulated-clock.why: The agents genuinely react to the time they are given. The same scheduler code runs against real wall clock time in production. Nothing here is pre-recorded.

verifier.title: The Verifier
verifier.plain: A separate agent that checks every statement before a human sees it, and rejects anything it cannot trace to the source document.
verifier.why: It means a sentence cannot appear on screen unless the evidence behind it is real. It also blocks instructions hidden inside a document, because an injected conclusion has no supporting quote.

quarantine.title: Quarantined text
quarantine.plain: Text inside an uploaded document that looked like an instruction rather than laboratory data, so it was removed before any AI read it.
quarantine.why: A document should describe facts, not give orders. What was removed is always shown rather than silently dropped.

critical-access.title: Critical access hospital
critical-access.plain: A small rural hospital, usually 25 beds or fewer, often the only one for a long distance.
critical-access.why: These hospitals may have limited infectious-disease support. CDC says that in most critical access hospitals a pharmacist, usually onsite, provides stewardship leadership.
critical-access.source: Critical Need: More Data on Antimicrobial Stewardship Programs in Critical Access Hospitals

wake-ladder.title: The wake ladder
wake-ladder.plain: The set of times this agent will wake up during one course of antibiotics, registered all at once when the patient is admitted.
wake-ladder.why: Registering everything up front means a crash cannot lose the rest of the course. The agent then sleeps, costing nothing, until each moment arrives.

registry.title: Agent Registry
registry.plain: A catalog where other departments in the hospital can find these agents, see what they produce, and consume them under controlled permissions.
registry.why: The antibiogram is useful to Infection Prevention and to the formulary committee, not only to pharmacy. Publishing it with versions and scopes is how that sharing stays governed.
registry.source: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agent Registry
